report.acquisition_coverage:
Own evidence only, about 7.3k queries charged.
- Pilot 1: profile of 4 groups x 7 conditions, schedule 8..4096. Only labels are usable: requesting 'checkpoint' or 'layer0_distance_evaluations' alongside the other features returned null for every other feature.
- Pilot 2: 1 group x 7 conditions, labels only (same issue).
- Pilot 3: feature check on 3 handles.
- Profile: 4 groups x 7 conditions, schedule [8..192], all 11 non-trivial features.
- Main acquisition: 50 groups x 7 conditions = 350 cases, schedule [4,8,12,16,24,32,48,64,96,128], 3,423 labelled frames. All seven conditions are equally represented.
- Evaluations: 2 groups x 7 (c1) and 14 unseen groups x 7 (c2).
Key facts measured:
- Traversal is filter-independent: layer-0 evaluations are identical across a group's filters, and native depth is set per group.
- Native ends between checkpoints 64 and about 200 (median about 11.7 ms; prefix at 128 is about 8.6 ms). Stopping beyond about 96 gains little.
- Labels are non-monotone in some v743/v527 cases.
- Recall failures dominate; count failures mostly occur in v743/v527.
- The search often stalls at 0.9 recall for many checkpoints, even with a positive frontier gap of up to 0.19, then improves late. This is why convergence features are unreliable.
Evidence comes from 66 of 450 development groups.
report.alternatives_considered:
Two distinct program structures were built and evaluated in two rounds.
(1) c1: a generic per-filter, per-checkpoint depth-3 tree from fit_policy. It used 10 features on the 10-checkpoint schedule S=[4..128]. Grouped 5-fold CV gave many false stops in every filter. Its exploratory evaluation on 2 groups x 7 conditions (14 cases) had 3 quality failures (unfiltered@12, v743@64, v310@48), despite about 40% measured savings.
(2) c2: a hand-built rule list fitted offline with schedule [16,32,64]. It stops when frontier_gap is above the maximum unsafe gap seen at checkpoints >= 0.75c, plus a 0.01 margin. Programs exist only for filters with >=2 training stops (unfiltered, 192, 108, 32); the other filters run pure native with no collection. On 14 unseen groups (98 cases) it had 1 failure: q0511-v32 stopped at 64 with recall 0.9 vs native 1.0. Its aggregate latency ratio vs native was 0.982 (90% CI 0.961-0.999); vs matched continuation it was 0.976. Controls did not pass, so these timings are inconclusive.
Offline analyses that were not fitted as candidates: consecutive-stable streak rules (top10_new==0 and tenth unchanged, k=1..4) combined with a minimum checkpoint and a gap threshold; relative-gap, gap/spread and frontier/first ratios; fixed per-filter checkpoints. None separated safe from unsafe frames for unfiltered, 108 or 32 without training false stops. The best zero-false streak rules for 743, 527, 310 and 192 saved only about 0.4-1.2 ms per case in-sample.
report.cost_evidence:
Collector overhead was measured in this run.
- Collecting all 11 features at 10 checkpoints: capture/native about 1.025 overall, up to 1.047 for unfiltered/v32. Clone and empty controls were about 1.00 ± 1-2%.
- c1's matched continuation (10 checkpoints, full features) was 1.031 vs native.
- c2's matched continuation (3 checkpoints, gap only, 4 filters) was 1.008 vs native.
- Acquisition costs about frames+3 queries per case; profile about 24 per case.
- Controls did not pass in any timing run, so every timing estimate here is diagnostic and inconclusive.
report.reason: ABSTAIN: no candidate qualified. Freezing requires zero native recall and count losses on all 3,150 development cases, plus controlled timing that beats both native and matched continuation. Both evaluated candidates had quality failures on held-out cases. The only stops that were zero-loss in training and gave a measurable saving (votes32) failed on held-out data. Without them, the remaining expected saving is about 0.5-1%, which the timing panel cannot resolve: control noise is about ±1-2%, and the c2 aggregate 90% CI already reached 0.999 even with the votes32 savings. I do not claim a win.
report.why_more_search_not_worth_cost: Remaining resources are about 42k discovery queries, of which about 24.8k are reserved for one full confirmation, and under $4 of model budget, with each further tool round costing roughly $0.5-1. The 98-case held-out failure rate (about 1 in 14 groups for votes32) implies about 30 expected failures across 450 groups. A zero-loss confirmation would therefore be very unlikely, and it would consume most of the remaining query budget. Making the rule safe enough would need several-fold more labelled groups to bound tail risk at about 1 in 3,000 cases. That is not affordable within the model/token budget, and even an ultra-conservative variant would save about 1% or less, below the measured control noise. Abstaining is the evidence-supported outcome; the open hypothesis is a much larger labelled sample for 108/32/unfiltered, plus a features-cost-aware rule using a 2-3 checkpoint schedule.
